run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T08:07:43Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy (otel-demo) is returning HTTP 500 at a high rate (about 55% of its ingress spans in the last 2 minutes of the window, up from ~0% at 08:08Z) because its upstream frontend cannot reach product-catalog. The frontend and checkout both fail their gRPC calls with '14 UNAVAILABLE ... connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080', and 100.69.9.250:8080 is the product-catalog Service ClusterIP. product-catalog has no running backend: the Deployment was rolled out at 08:07:56-08:08:03Z to a new ReplicaSet whose image is quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, the previous working pod (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) was stopped and deleted, and the new pod cannot pull the image ('401 UNAUTHORIZED' from quay.io), staying Pending in ImagePullBackOff with 0 ready/available replicas, so the Service endpoints list contains only a not-ready address. Error routes are exactly the product-catalog-dependent ones (product detail, recommendations, checkout), while cart and /api/data routes still succeed.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error spans are HTTP 500 on span_name 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' (status tags error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR); its 1h cumulative increase of ERROR spans rose from ~7 at 08:07:43Z to ~4,573 per series by 08:23:13Z.

The frontend-proxy ingress error-span ratio was ~0% (0-0.16%) through 08:08Z, jumped to 24.7% at the 08:10Z evaluation and held at ~55-58% from 08:12Z onward (latest 2m value 55.6%); a 5m evaluation ending 08:23:14Z gives 54.66%.

Sampled frontend-proxy error traces show its 500 spans are the ingress/egress spans of the same trace as frontend spans with http.status_code 500, i.e. the 500 originates from the frontend upstream, not from the proxy process.

Frontend traces failing GET /api/products/{productId} carry the exception message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080 - Local (0.0.0.0:0)' on 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' and on client span 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' with rpc.grpc.status_code 14; the visible parent references chain load-generator GET -> frontend-proxy ingress -> router frontend egress -> frontend GET -> GET /api/products/{productId} -> api route -> grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct.
Service product-catalog in otel-demo has clusterIP 100.69.9.250 and port 8080, exactly the address the failing frontend and checkout gRPC clients dial.
The product-catalog Service has zero ready endpoints: the endpoints object lists addresses [] and notReadyAddresses [100.96.4.116], which is the IP of the Pending product-catalog pod.

Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk (owned by ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966, created 2026-11-15T08:08:11Z) is phase Pending, container ready=false, restartCount 0, waiting reason ImagePullBackOff.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog is at 1 desired, updatedReplicas=1, but readyReplicas and availableReplicas are null, and its pod-template image is quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0; it is the only Deployment in the cluster whose ready replicas are below desired.

Kubernetes events show the rollout and the pull failure: 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-56fbb5f966 from 0 to 1' at 08:07:56Z, 'Scheduled' and 'Pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0"' at 08:07:56-08:07:58Z, 'Failed to pull image ... failed to resolve image: unexpected status from HEAD request to https://quay.io/v2/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid/manifests/1.0.0: 401 UNAUTHORIZED' and 'Error: ErrImagePull' at 08:07:59Z, 'Error: ImagePullBackOff' (21 occurrences, 08:08:16Z-08:13:26Z), plus 'Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0', 'Stopping container product-catalog' and 'Deleted pod: product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548' at 08:08:03Z.

ReplicaSet history confirms an image swap: product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 07:34:22Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) is now at replicas 0, while product-catalog-56fbb5f966 (created 08:07:55Z, image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0) is the current ReplicaSet with no ready pod.

product-catalog's own server spans stopped: the rate of 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' was ~7-15 spans/s through 08:10:00Z and 0 from 08:11:00Z onward, and 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' dropped to 0 at the same time; over the 20m to 08:23:14Z these spans were previously recorded with STATUS_CODE_UNSET (3,191.76 and 248.56), i.e. the service stopped serving rather than returning errors.

Over the 20m to 08:23:14Z frontend recorded 3,472 ERROR spans on 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct', 660 on 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' and 421 on 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', with per-2m client error rates for those spans starting at the 08:11:00Z evaluation point; recommendation recorded 664 ERROR spans on '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' and 664 on 'get_product_list', and checkout 414 each on 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder'.

checkout is affected on its own evidence: its span 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' has otel.status_description 'connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.69.9.250:8080: connect: operation not permitted"' (rpc.grpc.status_code 14), and its 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' span fails with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and description 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #...'.

Impact at route level in the 10m to 08:23:14Z: frontend 'GET /api/products/{productId}' = 2,013 ERROR vs 0 UNSET, 'GET /api/recommendations' = 401 ERROR vs 0 UNSET and 'POST /api/checkout' = 234 ERROR vs 0 UNSET, i.e. essentially all traffic on those routes fails, while 'GET /api/cart' (385.5 spans), 'GET /api/data' (364.2) and 'POST /api/cart' (750.8) show 0 error spans.

Timing of the observed anomaly versus the alert anchor differs: the alert anchor is 08:07:43Z, the failing rollout events start 08:07:56Z, the old product-catalog pod is deleted at 08:08:03Z, and the frontend-proxy error-span ratio is still ~0-0.13% at the 08:08Z/08:09Z evaluations, only rising at 08:10Z.

No NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace otel-demo (empty list), so a NetworkPolicy blocking frontend/checkout egress to product-catalog is not supported by the cluster state observed at query time.

frontend-proxy's pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-zj87n is Running, ready=true with restartCount 0, and its error spans are the ingress/egress spans of the same traces whose frontend spans carry the 500, so the proxy relays an upstream failure rather than failing itself.

cart was checked and shows no failure evidence: in the sampled checkout traces its server spans 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'HGET' were recorded without error tags and checkout's client 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' span carried rpc.grpc.status_code 0, while the 20m per-service ERROR-span breakdown returned no cart series; cart's pod cart-755465879b-vtpl9 is Running with 0 restarts.

Hypothesis that frontend-proxy itself broke or was restarted during the window is rejected: its pod shows 0 restarts and no waiting/termination reason, and every 500 it emitted in the sampled traces is a response relayed from the frontend upstream.

Hypothesis that the connect failures were caused by a NetworkPolicy or a registry-wide image-pull outage is not supported: no NetworkPolicy objects exist in otel-demo, only the product-catalog Deployment is short of ready replicas, and the failing image is a distinct 'hello-bench-invalid' quay.io repository (401 UNAUTHORIZED) while every other pod, including those on ghcr.io images, is Running and ready.

Root cause: the product-catalog Deployment's pod template was changed to the non-existent image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0; the rollout stopped and deleted the working 2.1.3 pod before the replacement could start, leaving the Service with no ready endpoint, so all callers dialing 100.69.9.250:8080 fail, frontend returns 500, and frontend-proxy relays that 500 (the alerting symptom).

Open candidate that is not the alert cause: small background error counts exist for ad (1.04 ERROR spans/20m) and fraud-detection (2.08) while accounting and payment returned 0; no evidence ties those to the frontend-proxy 500s, so they remain unattributed.

Restore the product-catalog Deployment to a pullable image (the previous ReplicaSet's ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) or point it at a valid image reference; the current image cannot be resolved (401 UNAUTHORIZED) and the pod will keep back-off retrying.

Review the product-catalog rollout strategy and readiness gating so a bad image cannot remove the last ready pod (the old pod was scaled to 0 and deleted at 08:08:03Z while the new pod never became ready), and add alerting on Deployment ready replicas and ImagePullBackOff for otel-demo.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what changed the product-catalog Deployment image, and when the change was applied, could not be verified.

The alert rule 'RequestErrorRate' was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (status no_data: a4487536-7b86-4e90-90c6-673be06d0cd6-t0:bc8d2e5b-f285-4403-b783-93e09cc6cd36), and the metric-name lookups for http_*/app_* and rpc_* returned no series (20fe2bb4-3517-4e8f-b4ab-d15865440868-t0:9f20d617-d8dc-4263-83e4-786a49aa2ee9, 8de87c38-8f9b-41d3-9964-60e15d41c598-t1:a4561468-063a-45a7-9b79-285dee194a11, 5701426c-f592-4a07-a45e-d5585a662120-t0:8b0c3184-8d26-4c88-8ecb-8608e1eccb94) and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count returned no data (52f03e14-b470-4140-a7d8-9f92492acc11-t0:caa1ae00-8954-4afa-9c1c-9b44da985ec9), so the rule's exact expression and the reported 'current: 18.18888888888889' value could not be reproduced; span-based frontend-proxy ingress ratios are 18.85% over the trailing hour and 54.66% over the last 5m at 08:23:14Z.

fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-gx54w returned no lines (status no_data: 7a8118f1-3574-4219-8537-023689a354ca-t0:2773b0ed-85f8-43cc-b8fc-ac7f4fb982cc), so frontend application log lines could not be read; the evidence for frontend's internal error comes from span exception fields instead.

The pending product-catalog pod never started a container, so no container logs or last termination reason exist for it, and the credential used (if any) to pull quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 cannot be read or verified.

Trace and span data are sampled views (three sampled trace views reported incomplete: 440db53d-1659-4d03-ba63-a888d071207f-t1:b62a100d-1948-4d74-a1f0-8a1b542a8a81, 5701426c-f592-4a07-a45e-d5585a662120-t1:0cd55d2d-5150-4896-abcc-c31e224d3f51, ff9a5a4d-281a-45fc-b6d1-054e69493e02-t0:a1860dd1-6cc7-4f97-b1ca-c5bbaac6ee04) and span counts are not unique request counts; the exact per-request error rate of frontend-proxy must come from the alerting metric, which was not available.
Kubernetes objects and the NetworkPolicy list reflect cluster state at query time (~08:24Z), not necessarily the incident moment, so the absence of NetworkPolicies then cannot be fully proven.
next_steps: Revert otel-demo/product-catalog to the last working image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) and confirm a pod reaches Running and the Service endpoint becomes ready.
Retrieve change/deployment history for otel-demo/product-catalog around 2026-11-15T08:07:5xZ to identify the actor and intent of the hello-bench-invalid image change.

After product-catalog is serving again, re-check the frontend-proxy error ratio and the frontend product-detail, recommendations and checkout routes to confirm recovery, and verify cart and other routes stayed healthy throughout.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
